topic: Emergency theatre delays and NCEPOD timing

audits.title: WTP7.11 CEPOD Booking Audit in General Surgery
audits.standard: Time to theatre within allotted CEPOD classification timeframe
audits.setting: Acute surgical unit, University Hospital of Southampton

cycle1.result: 632 (85%) achieved the time frame; 116 (15%) delayed, of which 94 (81%) were appropriately booked.

audits.other_findings: In a third of delays no reason was recorded; no difference in postoperative length of stay or unexpected findings.
audits.citation: Kitsikosta L, Diaz M, Galides C, Morsi M, Morrison-Jones V, Berry D. WTP7.11 CEPOD Booking Audit in General Surgery. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.227.

audits.title: EGS P34 CEPOD Booking Audit in General Surgery
audits.setting: Acute Surgical Unit, University Hospital Southampton

cycle1.result: 638 (84%) achieved the desired time frame; 122 (16%) delayed; 99/122 (81%) appropriately booked.

audits.other_findings: No reason recorded for one third of delays; no difference in median post-operative stay or unexpected findings.
audits.citation: Kitsikosta L, Diaz M, Galides C, Morsi M, Morrison-Jones V, Rahman S, et al.. EGS P34 CEPOD Booking Audit in General Surgery. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad348.080.

audits.title: 1178 A Study to Audit the Breach of CEPOD Guidelines in Emergency General and Colorectal Surgeries
audits.standard: Local CEPOD guidelines for time from booking to surgery
audits.setting: General and colorectal surgery department, Leicester Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Overall 28% breached CEPOD time to surgery: abscesses 27% (of 30), appendicectomies 30% (of 33), colorectal operations 33% (of 21). By category: 18% of category 2, 31% of category 3, 26% of category 4, 37% of category 5 breached.

audits.other_findings: Of colorectal operations, 67% required bowel resection and 43% needed a stoma.
audits.citation: Blinkhorn-Conroy O, Hussain I, Rahman K, Wong Sik Hee J, Tun San N, Norwood M. 1178 A Study to Audit the Breach of CEPOD Guidelines in Emergency General and Colorectal Surgeries. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.419.

audits.title: Decreasing delays in urgent and expedited surgery in a university teaching hospital through audit and communication between peri-operative and surgical directorates.
audits.standard: NCEPOD guidelines for urgent surgery: fully staffed emergency theatre and after-midnight operating restricted to immediate life-, limb- or organ-threatening conditions; classification of delays developed from existing guidelines
audits.setting: University teaching hospital, Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Trust (Freeman Hospital)

cycle1.result: Urgent cases continued to be delayed unnecessarily; incidence of delays audited (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Audit results disseminated to the involved perioperative and surgical directorates.

cycle2.result: Significant decrease in delays (p = 0.001), significant increase in surgeon availability (p = 0.001) and significant decrease in median waiting time for urgent surgery compared with the first cycle and a previous standard (p < 0.01).

audits.other_findings: An earlier audit had shown shorter waits and more senior care after overnight preoperative assessment by anaesthetic trainees.
audits.citation: Cosgrove JF, Gaughan M, Snowden CP, Lees T. Decreasing delays in urgent and expedited surgery in a university teaching hospital through audit and communication between peri-operative and surgical directorates. Anaesthesia. 2008;63(6):599-603. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2044.2008.05441.x. PMID: 18477270.

audits.title: Theatre delay for general surgical emergencies: a prospective audit.

cycle1.result: Operations after midnight 29 (21.3%); operating 0900-1700 40 (29.4%); median delay for appendicectomy 4 hrs 40 mins and abscess drainage 5 hrs 56 mins.

audits.intervention: Introduction of a fully staffed 24-hour emergency theatre.

cycle2.result: Operations after midnight 7 (6.3%); 0900-1700 71 (61.3%); median delay appendicectomy 1 hr 29 mins and abscess drainage 1 hr 51 mins (p < 0.01).

audits.other_findings: Commonest cause of delay remained queuing for theatre; no change in seniority of decision-maker.
audits.citation: Magee TR, Galland RB, Ramesh S, Dehn TC. Theatre delay for general surgical emergencies: a prospective audit. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 1995;77(3 Suppl):121-124. PMID: 7574304.
